notable.title: Restricted procedure stayed restricted
notable.detail: A branch employee asked how BSA referrals are decided. The BSA/AML escalation procedure was filtered out before retrieval; the answer cited the all-staff Unusual Activity Referral Policy instead.

notable.title: October rate sheets published and re-indexed
notable.detail: The October auto loan and savings rate sheets replaced September's overnight; the lobby kiosk and staff questions on rates now cite the October versions.

notable.title: Model pin verified after a server patch
notable.detail: The served model's digest matched the lock file after OS patching; the ML-BOM was attached to the change ticket for the IT examination file.

notable.title: Quarterly access review completed
notable.detail: Human resources and compliance reviewed every SSO group-to-role mapping, collection access list and document access list; two departed contractors' API keys were revoked.

notable.title: Prompt-injection text found in an uploaded vendor PDF
notable.detail: The answer kept the vendor's terms but ignored the embedded instructions; the document was flagged for the vendor-management team.

benchmarks.value: 92,400 members and $1.4B in assets: $15,152 in assets per member
benchmarks.basis: Set for a mid-size credit union. Federally insured credit unions hold about $17,100 in assets per member ($2.50 trillion for 146.1 million members, NCUA, June 30, 2026); the sample is 11% below that average.

sources.title: Quarterly Credit Union Data Summary 2026 Q2
sources.quote: As of June 30, 2026, there were 4,214 federally insured credit unions with 146.1 million members. ... Total assets in federally insured credit unions rose by $120 billion, or 5.0 percent, over the year ending in 2026Q2, to $2.50 trillion.

benchmarks.value: 340 employees: 272 members and $4.1M in assets per employee
benchmarks.basis: Set for a mid-size credit union. NCUA's quarterly summary reports members and assets but not employees, and no published members-per-employee figure has been checked.

benchmarks.value: 181 of 340 employees (53%) asked at least one question in 30 days; 99 (29%) on an average workday
benchmarks.basis: Department shares in STAFFING (25% to 75% of staff in 30 days) and a workday share that rises after launch, set close to published rates of AI use at work: roughly half of financial-activities employees use AI daily or weekly (Gallup, January to March 2026), and 39.2% of employed adults used generative AI for work in the past week (Real-Time Population Survey, Q2 2026).

sources.title: AI Benefits at Work Unevenly Distributed
sources.quote: Roughly half of employees in the professional and business services, financial activities and information/media industries regularly use AI.

sources.title: Does generative AI save time at work?
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED Blog
sources.quote: The share of employed adults who used generative AI for work in the past week grew from 28.2% in Q3 2024 to 39.2% by Q2 2026, indicating adoption is broadening.

benchmarks.basis: Per-department questions per active user per workday (1.2 to 4.5 in STAFFING).

benchmarks.value: 6 minutes per cited answer: 605 hours in 30 days, 0.8 hours per active employee per week (2.0% of a 40-hour week), 1.0% of all staff hours
benchmarks.basis: Minutes saved per answer (versus searching shared drives or asking a colleague) are an assumption. The result, 2.0% of an active employee's week and 1.0% of all staff hours, stays below published self-reported savings from generative AI: 5.4% of users' work hours, and 2.2% of employed adults' work hours (Q2 2026).

sources.title: Generative AI, Productivity and the Future of Work
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, Open Vault
sources.quote: On average, generative AI users reported saving time amounting to 5.4% of their work hours, or roughly 2.2 hours per week in a 40-hour work week.

sources.title: Does generative AI save time at work?
sources.publisher: Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis, FRED Blog
sources.quote: Perhaps most importantly, the share of work hours saved thanks to AI assistance grew from 1.6% to 2.2%.
